summary: Defines a MIB module for monitoring and controlling HPR (High Performance Routing) devices that can communicate in IP networks, in the IBM APPN world.

eli5.summary: This is a set of standard dials for old IBM-style network equipment that can now also send messages over the internet.

questions: what is the hpr ip mib
what is apn hpr over ip
how are appn traffic types mapped to tos precedence
subtitle: SNMP objects for counting and prioritizing APPN traffic that HPR devices carry over IP as UDP packets.

tldr.problem: APPN/HPR nodes can communicate over IP networks, but there was no standard way to monitor that traffic or to set how it maps onto IP precedence.
tldr.mechanism: The HPR-IP-MIB module counts UDP packets per link station and APPN traffic type, and holds tables for reading and setting the mapping from traffic types to the three TOS Precedence bits, per port with link station and connection network overrides.
tldr.outcome: Managers can watch and tune HPR over IP using SNMP. It is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata shows no replacement.

today: RFC 2584 is a Proposed Standard from May 1999, and the metadata for this unit lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.content:
RFC 2584 is a product of the SNA NAU Services MIB Working Group. It defines a MIB module for managing devices with HPR in IP networks capability. HPR (High Performance Routing) is an enhancement to the Advanced Peer-to-Peer Network (APPN) architecture that provides fast data routing and improved session reliability. APPN is the part of Systems Network Architecture (SNA) that supports peer-to-peer networking.

APPN/HPR in IP Networks, described in RFC 2353, is a further enhancement that lets APPN/HPR nodes communicate over IP. General APPN management information is in the APPN MIB, and HPR management information is in the HPR MIB, RFC 2238.
sections.eli5: Some older company computer networks can now send their messages over the internet. This document says how to check on and adjust that.

sections.title: What the MIB Covers
sections.content:
The module has two highlights. It counts UDP packets sent with each type of APPN traffic on HPR/IP links, and it lets a manager monitor and set the mapping between APPN traffic types and the TOS Precedence settings in the IP header. The text notes that RFC 2474 redefined these as the first three bits of the differentiated services code point (DSCP).

It does not support configuring the IP addresses used for APPN ports or link stations.
sections.eli5: It has two jobs: counting how many packets of each kind were sent, and choosing how important each kind is to the internet.

sections.title: How It Fits the APPN MIB
sections.content:
The APPN MIB identifies ports and link stations with three objects: appnPortDlcType, appnLsDlcType and appnLsStatusDlcType. When they identify an HPR/IP port or link station they return the IANAifType value 126, defined as "IP (for APPN HPR in IP networks)".

The IP addresses are returned in appnPortDlcLocalAddr, appnLsLocalAddr, appnLsRemoteAddr, appnLsStatusLocalAddr and appnLsStatusRemoteAddr, as ASCII text using the DisplayableDlcAddress convention. The objects appnPortSpecific and appnLsSpecific should return a RowPointer to the matching ifEntry in the agent's ifTable.
sections.eli5: The older list marks IP links with a special number, 126, so you know a link goes over the internet.

sections.title: Traffic Types and Tables
sections.content:
The textual convention AppnTrafficType has five values: low (1), medium (2), high (3), network (4) and llcAndFnRoutedNlp (5). The first four match APPN transmission priorities. The fifth covers LLC commands (XID, TEST, DISC and DM) and function-routed NLPs (XID_DONE_RQ and XID_DONE_RSP).

The monitoring group has one table, hprIpActiveLsTable, indexed by link station name and traffic type. Its counter hprIpActiveLsUdpPackets counts outgoing UDP packets carrying that traffic type. The configuration group has three tables: hprIpAppnPortTable, hprIpLsTable and hprIpCnTable.
sections.eli5: Messages come in five kinds, from low to network control. The MIB keeps a count for each kind on each link.

sections.title: TOS Precedence Mapping and Overrides
sections.content:
The AppnTOSPrecedence convention is a three-character string for the TOS Precedence bits. The HPR over IP architecture's default mapping is: network 110, high 100, medium 010, low 001, and LLC commands and similar traffic 110.

The mapping is set per port. A link station or a connection network can override it with its own entry. With no entry, it inherits the port's mapping. A Set on the port value takes effect immediately, without waiting for the port or node to reinitialize.
sections.eli5: Each kind of message gets a priority sticker. You choose stickers for a whole port, and a single link can pick different ones if it needs to.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The MIB reports no passwords or user data, but some enterprises treat network configuration and usage as corporate assets and may want to restrict SNMP access. Authentication of SNMP requests and controlled access SHOULD be used in such environments.

The one read-write and four read-create objects can affect network operations, so restricting SNMP access to them is recommended. The text warns that a bad mapping can cause delays or disruptions. For example, mapping APPN traffic type High to the same bits as bulk data gives network control traffic the same precedence as bulk data, which may delay session initialization and cause timeouts on control sessions.
sections.eli5: If someone gives the important messages a low-priority sticker, the network can slow down or break, so only trusted people should be allowed to change the stickers.
